$comment: Percent-encoded unreserved characters are decoded (URL-CANONICALIZATION.md §3.3.4 rule 6). RFC 3986 §2.3 lists ALPHA / DIGIT / - . _ ~ as unreserved; their percent-encoded form is semantically identical to the literal byte. P emits %41/bar, A receives A/bar; both decode to A/bar.
name: unreserved-decoded
scenario: Naive HTTP client emits %41 for 'A'; modern proxy decodes to literal byte
$comment_reserved: Contrast: %2F (the slash, RFC 3986 §2.2 reserved) stays %2F under rule 7. Decoding it would change the request target (slash is a path separator). See percent-encoding-case.json.
